title: datefixR: Comprehensive Date Standardization Guide
text: datefixR comprehensive R package designed automatically standardize messy date data consistent, machine-readable formats. Whether ’re dealing mixed date formats web forms, international datasets, legacy systems, datefixR intelligently parses diverse date representations converts R’s standard Date class.

title: datefixR: Comprehensive Date Standardization Guide
text: Smart parsing: Handles mixed date formats, separators, representations single dataset Multilingual support: Recognizes dates English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Czech, Slovak, Indonesian Missing data imputation: User-controlled behavior incomplete dates (missing days/months) Detailed error reporting: Identifies exactly dates couldn’t parsed Excel compatibility: Supports R Excel numeric date representations Roman numeral support: Experimental support Roman numeral months

title: datefixR: Comprehensive Date Standardization Guide
text: Firstly, demonstrate date standardization without imputation. consider data frame two columns dates differing formats missing data. fix_date_df() requires two arguments, df, data frame (tibble) object col.names, character vector containing names columns standardized. default, first column data frame assumed contain row IDs. IDs used warning error raised assist user locating source error. ID column can also manually provided via id argument. output function data frame tibble (dependent object type first argument, df) selected date columns now standardized belonging Date class. datefixR can handle many different formats including -, /, ., white space separation, year-first day-first, month supplied number, abbreviation full length name. fix_date_char() similar fix_date_df() applies single character object.
code: bad.dates <- data.frame(   id = seq(5),   some.dates = c(     "02/05/92",     "01-04-2020",     "1996/05/01",     "2020-05-01",     "02-04-96"   ),   some.more.dates = c(     "01 03 2015",     "2nd January 2010",     "01/05/1990",     "03-Dec-2012",     "02 April 2020"   ) ) knitr::kable(bad.dates) fixed.dates <- fix_date_df(   bad.dates,   c("some.dates", "some.more.dates") ) knitr::kable(fixed.dates) fix_date_char("01 02 2014") #> [1] "2014-02-01"

title: datefixR: Comprehensive Date Standardization Guide
text: datefixR currently supports dates provided English, Français (French), Deutsch (German), español (Spanish), Русский (Russian) recognizing names months languages formatting customs. Expected languages need specified can provided just like date standardized. Functions datefixR assume day-first instead month-first day, month, year given numerically (unless year given first). However, behavior can modified passing format = "mdy" function calls. month given name, datefixR automatically detect correct format without format argument needing specified user.
code: fix_date_char("7 de septiembre del 2014") #> [1] "2014-09-07" fix_date_char("01 02 2014", format = "mdy") #> [1] "2014-01-02" fix_date_char("July 4th, 1776") #> [1] "1776-07-04"

title: datefixR: Comprehensive Date Standardization Guide
text: default, datefixR imputes missing months July, missing days month first day. , “1992” converts argument defaulting July 1st-2nd July halfway year (non leap year). Therefore, assuming year supplied indeed correct, imputation maximum potential error 6 months true date. However, behavior can changed supplying day.impute month.impute arguments integer corresponding desired day month. example, day.impute = 1 month.impute = 1 results first day January imputed instead often common imputation missing date data. imputation mechanism can also modified impute NA month day missing setting day.impute month.impute NA. also result warning raised. Finally, imputation can prevented setting day.impute month.impute NULL. result error raised day month missing respectively. day.impute month.impute can also passed fix_date_df() similar functionality.
code: fix_date_char("1992") #> [1] "1992-07-01" fix_date_char("1992", day.impute = 1, month.impute = 1) #> [1] "1992-01-01" fix_date_char("1992", month.impute = NA) #> [1] NA fix_date_char("1992", month.impute = NULL) # ERROR example.df <- data.frame(   id = seq(1, 3),   some.dates = c("2014", "April 1990", "Mar 19") ) fix_date_df(example.df, "some.dates", day.impute = 1, month.impute = 1) #>   id some.dates #> 1  1 2014-01-01 #> 2  2 1990-04-01 #> 3  3 2019-03-01

title: datefixR: Comprehensive Date Standardization Guide
text: datefixR implements intelligent two-digit year expansion using sliding window approach. algorithm examines first digit two-digit year compares third digit current year. Algorithm Details: - first digit ≤ current year’s third digit: prefix “20” - first digit > current year’s third digit: prefix “19” Edge Case Behavior: time progresses, window shifts naturally. 2030, years 00-30 map 2000-2030, 31-99 map 1931-1999.

title: Convert non-standardized dates to R's Date class — fix_date_char
code: # Basic usage bad.date <- "02 03 2021" fix_date_char(bad.date) #> [1] "2021-03-02"  # Multiple formats with different separators mixed_dates <- c(   "02/05/92", # slash separator, 2-digit year   "2020-may-01", # hyphen separator, text month   "1996.05.01", # dot separator   "02 04 96", # space separator   "le 3 mars 2013" # French format ) fix_date_char(mixed_dates) #> [1] "1992-05-02" "2020-05-01" "1996-05-01" "1996-04-02" "2013-03-03"  # Text months in different languages text_months <- c(   "15 January 2020", # English   "15 janvier 2020", # French   "15 Januar 2020", # German   "15 enero 2020", # Spanish   "15 de janeiro de 2020" # Portuguese ) fix_date_char(text_months) #> [1] "2020-01-15" "2020-01-15" "2020-01-15" "2020-01-15" "2020-01-15"  # Roman numeral months (experimental) roman_dates <- c("15.VII.2023", "3.XII.1999", "1.I.2000") fix_date_char(roman_dates, roman.numeral = TRUE) #> [1] "2023-07-15" "1999-12-03" "2000-01-01"  # Excel serial numbers excel_serials <- c("44197", "44927") # Excel dates fix_date_char(excel_serials, excel = TRUE) #> [1] "2021-01-01" "2023-01-01"  # Two-digit years (automatic century detection) two_digit_years <- c("15/03/99", "15/03/25", "15/03/50") fix_date_char(two_digit_years) # 1999, 2025, 1950 #> [1] "1999-03-15" "2025-03-15" "1950-03-15"  # MDY format (US style) us_dates <- c("12/25/2023", "07/04/1776", "02/29/2020") fix_date_char(us_dates, format = "mdy") #> [1] "2023-12-25" "1776-07-04" "2020-02-29"  # Incomplete dates with custom imputation incomplete <- c("2023", "March 2022", "June 2021") fix_date_char(incomplete, day.impute = 15, month.impute = 6) #> [1] "2023-06-15" "2022-03-15" "2021-06-15"
